definition: Meritorious means deserving of reward or formal recognition because of genuine merit or achievement.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word meritorious. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know meritorious should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The judges reserved the top prize for truly meritorious work, not merely polished work.
Decent work is acceptable and no more; meritorious work rises far enough above that to have genuinely earned a reward.
Heroic goes beyond meritorious, suggesting achievement at real personal risk or sacrifice.

Praiseworthy work deserves spoken praise — compliments, applause, approving words. Meritorious sets the bar higher: the achievement has earned actual reward or formal recognition, a prize or a medal rather than a pat on the back. Praiseworthy work earns words; meritorious work earns the trophy.

Admirable describes anything worthy of respect and approval — a person's patience, courage, or taste can all be admirable. Meritorious is narrower and more official: it points at a deed or piece of work whose concrete achievement has earned a reward. You admire character; you reward meritorious work.
